points.title: 成长与教育
points.description: 菲茨杰拉德出生于圣保罗一个中产阶级家庭，父亲是家具商，母亲是爱尔兰裔富商之女。他在这里度过了童年和青少年时期，接受了良好的私立教育。这段经历塑造了他对上流社会的向往与矛盾态度，同时也培养了他的文学天赋。1908-1911年他在纽曼学校就读，开始尝试写作，并在校刊上发表作品。这段时期的生活经历为他后来的创作提供了丰富的素材，特别是对阶级差异和社会流动性的观察。
points.descriptionEn: Born into a middle-class family in Saint Paul, Fitzgerald had a comfortable yet somewhat unstable upbringing. His father was a furniture manufacturer from Maryland, while his mother came from a wealthy Irish immigrant family. This duality of backgrounds influenced his later writing about class and social mobility. He attended the Newman School (1908-1911) where he began writing seriously and published his first stories in the school magazine. These formative years in Saint Paul provided him with material for his later works and shaped his complex relationship with the upper class.

points.title: 大学岁月
points.description: 菲茨杰拉德进入普林斯顿大学，但并未完成学业。在普林斯顿，他积极参与校园文学活动，成为《普林斯顿人》杂志的编辑，并与未来的著名批评家爱德蒙·威尔逊成为好友。这段时期他创作了大量短篇小说和剧本，但学业成绩不佳，最终于1917年退学参军。普林斯顿的经历对他至关重要，不仅培养了他的文学才能，也让他接触到了东海岸上流社会的文化氛围，这成为他日后创作的重要背景。他在这里开始构思《人间天堂》，这部作品后来奠定了他的文学地位。
points.descriptionEn: Fitzgerald attended Princeton University but never graduated. There, he became actively involved in literary activities, serving as an editor for the Princeton Tiger literary magazine and forming a lifelong friendship with critic Edmund Wilson. He wrote numerous short stories and plays during this period but struggled academically. Despite his withdrawal in 1917 to join the army, Princeton was crucial for his development as a writer. It exposed him to East Coast high society culture, which would later feature prominently in his works, and it was here that he began构思 his first novel, This Side of Paradise, which would establish his literary reputation.

points.title: 成名与爵士时代
points.description: 1920年，菲茨杰拉德的第一部小说《人间天堂》出版，一炮而红，使他成为美国文坛的新星。同年他与泽尔达·塞尔结婚，两人成为纽约社交圈的明星。在纽约期间，他频繁出入高级俱乐部和宴会，沉浸于爵士时代的浮华生活。1922年出版《美丽与毁灭》，进一步巩固了他的文学地位。然而，这种奢华生活也给他带来了经济压力和创作困境。纽约的经历为他提供了丰富的创作素材，但也让他深刻体会到了美国梦的虚幻与幻灭，这些主题后来成为他作品的核心。
points.descriptionEn: In 1920, Fitzgerald's first novel, This Side of Paradise, was published to critical and commercial success, establishing him as a rising star in American literature. He married Zelda Sayre the same year, and the couple became fixtures in New York's social scene. During this period, Fitzgerald immersed himself in the Jazz Age's extravagance, frequenting exclusive clubs and parties. His second novel, The Beautiful and Damned, appeared in 1922, further cementing his reputation. However, this lavish lifestyle created financial pressures and creative challenges. New York provided rich material for his writing while exposing him to the illusions and disillusionments of the American Dream, themes that would become central to his work.

points.title: 欧洲创作高峰
points.description: 1924年，菲茨杰拉德移居巴黎，成为美国'迷惘的一代'作家群体的一员。在巴黎，他与海明威、格特鲁德·斯坦因等作家交往密切，文学创作达到高峰。1925年，他的代表作《了不起的盖茨比》出版，这部作品被公认为美国文学经典，深刻探讨了美国梦的幻灭。在巴黎期间，他生活相对稳定，创作精力充沛，同时也开始酗酒问题。这段欧洲经历开阔了他的国际视野，使他的作品超越了单纯的美国背景，具有了更普遍的人性探索。巴黎的岁月成为他创作生涯中最富有成果的时期之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1924, Fitzgerald moved to Paris, becoming part of the circle of American 'Lost Generation' writers including Hemingway and Gertrude Stein. This period marked his creative peak. His masterpiece, The Great Gatsby, was published in 1925 and is now considered a classic of American literature, exploring the illusions of the American Dream. In Paris, Fitzgerald enjoyed relative stability and creative productivity, though his drinking problems began to surface. His European experiences broadened his perspective beyond American settings, allowing for more universal explorations of human nature. The Paris years represent one of the most productive periods of his literary career.

points.title: 晚年与好莱坞
points.description: 1937年，菲茨杰拉德移居好莱坞，为米高梅等电影公司担任编剧工作。这是他人生最后的阶段，也是他经济最困难的时期。尽管创作力衰退，但他仍在1940年完成了最后一部未完成小说《最后的大亨》。在好莱坞期间，他与泽尔达的关系进一步恶化，泽尔达精神疾病加重，最终在1948年去世。菲茨杰拉德本人于1940年因心脏病去世，年仅44岁。好莱坞的经历让他接触到了美国流行文化的另一面，也让他反思了艺术与商业的关系。晚年的他虽然经济拮据，但仍在坚持写作，展现了作家对艺术的执着追求。
points.descriptionEn: In 1937, Fitzgerald moved to Hollywood, where he worked as a screenwriter for MGM and other studios. This final phase of his life was marked by financial difficulties and declining creativity. Despite these challenges, he completed his last unfinished novel, The Last Tycoon, in 1940. In Hollywood, his relationship with Zelda deteriorated further as her mental health declined (she would eventually die in 1948). Fitzgerald himself died of a heart attack in 1940 at age 44. His Hollywood experience exposed him to another facet of American popular culture and prompted reflections on the relationship between art and commerce. Despite his hardships, he remained committed to writing until his death, demonstrating his enduring dedication to his craft.

appraisal.zh: 菲茨杰拉德被公认为美国现代文学的重要代表，名字与「爵士时代」紧密相连；他以优美精炼、富于诗意的文笔开创美国现代小说新风格，《了不起的盖茨比》深刻揭示美国梦的虚幻，他本人也是敏锐的社会观察者，作品至今影响当代文学。另一种看法认为，他的主题重复、过度聚焦上流社会的奢华而少及更广的社会问题，酗酒等个人放纵损害了创作，女性角色常被指刻板，后期作品也显出创造力衰退。
appraisal.en: Fitzgerald is widely recognized as a pivotal figure in American modern literature, his name bound to the Jazz Age; his elegant, lyrical prose opened a new style for American fiction, The Great Gatsby probes the illusory nature of the American Dream, and he was a keen social observer whose work still influences contemporary writing. Another view holds that his themes repeat, that he dwelt on the glamour of the wealthy rather than broader social issues, that heavy drinking damaged his output, that his female characters are often called stereotyped, and that his later work shows declining creative vitality.

supporter.zh: 菲茨杰拉德被誉为'爵士时代的代言人'，他的作品捕捉了20世纪20年代美国社会的浮华与幻灭。他的文学语言优美精炼，具有诗意的抒情性，开创了美国现代小说的新风格。《了不起的盖茨比》被公认为美国文学经典，深刻探讨了美国梦的虚幻本质。菲茨杰拉德不仅是一位杰出的小说家，也是一位敏锐的社会观察者，他的作品至今仍对当代文学产生深远影响。
supporter.en: Fitzgerald is celebrated as the 'chronicler of the Jazz Age,' whose works captured the glamour and disillusionment of 1920s America. His elegant and lyrical prose style revolutionized American fiction, and The Great Gatsby is regarded as a masterpiece exploring the illusory nature of the American Dream. Beyond his technical skill, Fitzgerald was a keen social observer whose insights into class, wealth, and aspiration remain relevant today. His influence on contemporary literature endures, making him one of America's most important 20th-century novelists.

critic.zh: 批评者指出菲茨杰拉德的作品主题重复，过度关注上流社会的奢华生活，缺乏对更广泛社会问题的关注。他的个人生活被批评为放纵不羁，酗酒问题严重影响了创作质量。此外，他的女性角色塑造常被批评为刻板和表面化，特别是对妻子泽尔达的描写存在争议。一些评论家认为他的后期作品未能达到早期的高度，显示出创作力的衰退。
critic.en: Critics argue that Fitzgerald's work suffers from thematic repetition, with excessive focus on the lifestyles of the wealthy rather than broader social issues. His personal life, marked by excessive drinking, is seen as having negatively impacted his creative output. Additionally, his female characters are often criticized as stereotyped and superficial, particularly his portrayal of Zelda. Some literary scholars contend that his later works failed to reach the heights of his early achievements, showing a decline in creative vitality as he struggled with personal and professional challenges.

objective.zh: 在历史和流行文化视角下，菲茨杰拉德被定义为美国现代文学的重要代表人物，他的名字与'爵士时代'紧密相连。他的作品不仅反映了特定历史时期的社会风貌，也探索了普遍的人性主题。流行文化中，菲茨杰拉德的形象常与浪漫化的'天才与毁灭'叙事相关联，他的个人悲剧与艺术成就交织在一起，成为美国文学神话的一部分。学术界对他的评价日益多元，既肯定其文学贡献，也承认其个人局限，展现了一个复杂而立体的文学形象。
objective.en: From historical and cultural perspectives, Fitzgerald is recognized as a pivotal figure in American modern literature, his name inextricably linked to the 'Jazz Age.' His works not only reflect a specific historical moment but also explore universal human themes. In popular culture, Fitzgerald is often romanticized as part of the 'tortured genius' narrative, where personal tragedy intersects with artistic achievement. Academically, his reputation has evolved to acknowledge both his significant literary contributions and personal limitations, presenting a complex and multifaceted figure in American literary history.

self.zh: 所以我们奋力向前划，逆流向上的小舟，不停地倒退，进入过去。
self.en: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
